headline: 7 killed as cylinder-laden van explodes in Ashulia
summary: An explosion in a covered van carrying gas cylinders sparked a deadly fire, with reports indicating some cylinders were expired.
details: A devastating explosion and subsequent fire involving a covered van carrying gas cylinders occurred in Ashulia, leaving at least 7 people dead.
The blast was so powerful that it caused widespread panic and destruction in the surrounding area.
Investigation into the wreckage revealed that some of the cylinders being transported were expired, with one cylinder explicitly marked 'Do not use after 2021'.
Survivors have expressed deep terror and trauma, describing the scene as an atmosphere of extreme panic.
Emergency services worked to contain the fire and manage the casualties following the blast.
caption:
7 people killed in a horrific blast. An expired gas cylinder was found at the scene.

A devastating explosion and subsequent fire involving a covered van carrying gas cylinders occurred in Ashulia, leaving at least 7 people dead.

The blast was so powerful that it caused widespread panic and destruction in the surrounding area.

Investigation into the wreckage revealed that some of the cylinders being transported were expired, with one cylinder explicitly marked 'Do not use after 2021'.

Survivors have expressed deep terror and trauma, describing the scene as an atmosphere of extreme panic.

Emergency services worked to contain the fire and manage the casualties following the blast.

headline_marked: BPC lost Tk 22,875cr in 6 months; [[Govt raises fuel prices by Tk 20]]
headline: BPC lost Tk 22,875cr in 6 months; Govt raises fuel prices by Tk 20
summary: Energy State Minister Anindya Islam Amit says the hike was unavoidable due to soaring international costs and unsustainable subsidies.
details: The government has increased the prices of diesel, octane, petrol, and kerosene by Tk 20 per litre each. Energy State Minister Anindya Islam Amit stated that the decision was necessary due to rising international costs and the risk of cross-border smuggling.
caption:
BPC lost Tk 22,875 crore in just six months. Now, fuel prices are up by Tk 20 per litre.

The government has increased the prices of diesel, octane, petrol, and kerosene by Tk 20 per litre each. Energy State Minister Anindya Islam Amit stated that the decision was necessary due to rising international costs and the risk of cross-border smuggling.

#Bangladesh #FuelPrice #Economy #BPC #Inflation

Source: The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo
